assertions.statement: Simulation environments and mid-level representations are used to train autonomous driving models on both real and simulated data.
This enables closed-loop simulation testing prior to real-world deployment.
The CARLA simulator is an open-source platform that supports the development, training, and validation of autonomous urban driving systems.
CARLA allows flexible specification of sensor suites and environmental conditions.
End-to-end learning approaches have been explored, including convolutional neural networks (CNNs) that learn the entire processing pipeline to steer a vehicle.
The CNN uses input from a single front-facing center camera.
CARLA has been used to study multiple autonomous driving approaches, including classic modular pipelines, end-to-end imitation learning, and end-to-end reinforcement learning.
ChauffeurNet is a recurrent neural network (RNN) that uses mid-level input representations to output driving trajectories for vehicle control.
